questions.question: Explain why a quadratic equation must be in the standard form ($ax^2 + bx + c = 0$) before you begin factoring.
questions.expected_answer: It must be set to zero so that after factoring, the zero-product property can be applied. The property only works if the product equals zero.

questions.question: When factoring by grouping, how do you know if you have made a mistake in the middle of the process?
questions.expected_answer: After factoring out the greatest common factor from both groups, the remaining binomials in the parentheses must be exactly identical. If they are not, an error was made.

questions.question: In your own words, describe how the zero-product property is used to find the final solutions of a factored quadratic equation.
questions.expected_answer: Once the equation is factored into two binomials multiplied together and set to zero, the property allows us to set each individual binomial equal to zero and solve them as simple linear equations.
